summary: The note surveys local music education and community outreach programs that began in autumn 2023 and aim to make music accessible to everyone. It covers school instruction, percussion workshops, an orchestra collaboration, music therapy, a songwriter showcase and a technology-focused festival series. Together they show how local musicians and educators serve the community's varied needs through inclusivity and innovation.
one_line: Overview of autumn 2023 local music education and outreach programs, from school lessons and percussion workshops to music therapy and tech-driven live events.
key_facts: The Learning Notes Program was established on October 10, 2023, by music educator Rose Franklin to teach music theory, instrumental practice and performance arts to children in underfunded school districts.
Rose Franklin and her team of music teachers visit schools three times weekly, bringing instruments from violins to electronic keyboards.
'The Beat Goes On' percussion workshops started on November 5, 2023, and are held every second Saturday in a converted warehouse on Fifth Street.
Percussionist Jamal Edwards leads 'The Beat Goes On', teaching drumbeats from West African djembe to Latin American congas along with their history and cultural significance.

'Strings Attached' is a partnership in which the local Symphony Orchestra, led by Maestro Elizabeth Hughes, has opened its rehearsal doors to music students and small independent artists since early September 2023.
'Strings Attached' began with an interactive concert series doubling as a masterclass, in which participants shared the stage with the orchestra.
The 'Soulful Sounds' program, begun October 15, 2023, by music therapist Laura Gibson, offers music therapy for people with mental health issues, disabilities, and those in palliative care.
Soulful Sounds sessions include songwriting, instrument playing, and music and movement activities.
Guitarist and event organizer John Stephens began the Singer-Songwriter Showcase on September 22, 2023; it is a bimonthly event for emerging vocalists and songwriters to perform original pieces.
Sound engineer Amy Chen launched the 'Future of Fest' series in late September 2023, featuring virtual reality music videos, sound beams for immersive audio and AI-assisted music composition.
Local live music includes open-air jazz sessions at the downtown plaza led by saxophonist Marcus Johnson and indie rock gigs at The Groove Hall by bands like 'Eclipse of Eden' and 'Neon Thread'.
